peers.source: Turner & Townsend Data Centre Construction Cost Index 2025-2026 (turnerandtownsend.com)
peers.caveat: Data-centre specific, but global rather than US. This is T&T's cost-index headline, not their separate tender price inflation metric.
peers.quote: an average 15 percent uplift in local currency construction costs (2022) | the overall average year-on-year cost increase across the index from 2022-2023 is six percent | the overall average year-on-year cost increase across the 2024 index is nine percent, compared to six percent in 2023 | 5.5 percent increase in the cost per watt (2025)

peers.caveat: US non-residential building of every type, not data centres. A bid-price proxy: Turner's published method includes the competitive condition of the marketplace, so bid climate and contractor margin sit inside the number — though Turner stops short of saying the series prices accepted tenders.
peers.quote: The Turner Building Cost Index is determined by the following factors considered on a nationwide basis: labor rates and productivity, material prices and the competitive condition of the marketplace. | YEAR / AVERAGE INDEX / % — 2025 1485 4.1 | 2024 1426 3.9 | 2023 1373 6.0 | 2022 1295 8.0 | 2021 1199 1.9 | 2020 1177 1.8 | 2019 1156 5.5 | 2018 1096 5.6

peers.publication: PPI by industry: new office building construction (PCU236223236223)
peers.asof: December 2025 final; series runs to June 2026, preliminary
peers.caveat: Office buildings, not data centres — the de facto deflator for DC capital plans because BLS publishes no data-centre construction PPI. An output-price index: it measures what contractors receive, not what inputs cost. Dec-over-Dec computed by us from the published index levels.
